questions.question: Finding 4: how should RFC A.2 handle S3's `a/` folder markers?

options.label: Driver maps to folder (Recommended)
options.description: The S3 driver reads a trailing-slash marker as a folder, not a raw key, so it never gives an empty name. This matches how S3 consoles create folders, and A.2 shows it as a driver-level mapping.

options.label: Undecodable
options.description: `a/` falls in the same group as `/a` and `a//b`: an empty name, no tree. This is simpler, but folders made with the S3 console then drop out of the tree.

questions.question: Finding 5: how should name equality be handled?

options.label: Scope + point to BK-436 (Recommended)
options.description: D4 and A.5's write column apply only to encodings that compare names exactly, with a pointer to BK-436. The RFC stays small and doesn't decide ahead of BK-436.

options.label: Add an A.2 property
options.description: Add a name-equality property to each A.2 encoding row now. This is more complete, but it partly decides BK-436 ahead of that item.

questions.question: S3 folder markers (`a/`) conflict with A.6. On S3, a delimiter listing reports the prefix `a/` whenever any raw key starts with it, the marker included, and `list_page("a/", limit=1)` sees the marker. So a marker with nothing else under it is observably an empty folder. A.6 and StoreTree.dfy §7 (`FlatFoldersHoldItems`) say a flat encoding holds none. Which wording should land?

options.label: Marker = folder, A.6 carve-out (Recommended)
options.description: The S3 driver maps `a/` to the folder `a`. It is the one raw key with an empty segment that decodes. A.6 gains: "a folder marker another tool wrote holds an empty folder on S3 until it is deleted; the library never writes one". StoreTree.dfy's 'Not modelled' line adds markers. This matches what S3 shows today, and no proof changes.

options.label: Marker = folder, no carve-out
options.description: Same mapping, but I don't touch A.6 and leave the conflict for BK-436 to measure. The RFC then states two things that disagree for a marker-only folder.

options.label: Back to undecodable
options.description: `a/` is omitted like `a//b`. A.6 stays as it is, but the parent listing still shows `a` as a prefix that then lists empty. The model would then disagree with what S3 observably does.

S3 folder markers. On moto with only `a/` stored: s3fs and pyarrow list it as an item `a`, and boto3 hides it. All three answer `DirectoryNotEmpty` for a non-recursive `delete_folder("a")`, and only a recursive one removes it. The carve-out you picked earlier doesn't hold against that. How should the RFC treat markers?

options.label: Stated limit, like A.3 (Recommended)
options.description: A marker `n/` (n with no empty segment) is a foreign raw entry the model doesn't decode, stated as a limit with today's answers. The folder `a` shows while the marker exists, `delete_folder(a)` answers `DirectoryNotEmpty`, and a recursive one removes it. A.6's carve-out goes and §7/§11 stay true. Impact gets a row: on the kernel, s3fs and pyarrow stop listing the marker as an item.

options.label: Marker = folder object
options.description: Model it fully: an S3 driver with markers declares a folder-objects property, and A.5 and A.8 get marker rows. Then `delete_folder(a)` on a marker-only folder removes it, which changes today's `DirectoryNotEmpty`. §11's `Possible` and §7 need edits and new proofs. That's a larger change, and the model gains an encoding quirk.

options.label: Undecodable after all
options.description: `a/` is omitted like `a//b`, and the folder `a` still shows through the parent's prefix while the marker exists. This is the simplest text, but it disagrees with all three backends' `is_folder("a") = True`.

questions.question: The `Name` restriction is declared but nothing checks it: all three mutants still verify. What should land?

options.label: Join + injectivity lemma (Recommended)
options.description: Add `Join(k: Key): string` and a lemma `Join(a) == Join(b) ==> a == b`, which needs both conditions. That makes TREE-010's string form a real proof, and a weakened `Name` would fail. About 30 lines of Dafny, plus mutants re-run for the trace.

options.label: Names conjunct in TrieWF
options.description: Add `forall s, i :: s in l && 0 <= i < |s| ==> |s[i]| > 0 && '/' !in s[i]` to TrieWF, so TreeIsTrie fails under `Name = string`. Smaller, but it checks only §12's tie, not TREE-010's joined string.

options.label: Reword only
options.description: The comments say the condition holds by declaration and no lemma depends on it. No proof is added.

questions.question: Name equality affects every A.5 column, not only writes (a case-insensitive `read("A")` finds `a`). Where should the scope go?

options.label: On resolution, in A.1 (Recommended)
options.description: One sentence in A.1: resolution, and so every A.5 column and A.4's checks, holds where the encoding compares names exactly, and other equalities are open under BK-436. D4, A.2 and A.5 point to it. One home for the scope.

options.label: On each section
options.description: Keep the A.2 paragraph and widen the A.5 sentence to all columns, and A.4 and D4 each get their own clause. More places to keep in sync.

answers.S3 folder markers. On moto with only `a/: to be checked before or when designing the driver: if S3 storage on aws allows for existing prefixes, that have no blob behind, than this is to be treated IMHO as empty folder

questions.question: Open question 1 (S3 markers) has no owner: no backlog item moves an S3 driver onto the kernel, and BK-394 is Memory only. Where should it live?

options.label: New BK item (Recommended)
options.description: I file one item: 'Flat folder markers and empty-segment raw keys have no decoding', after BK-394, with RFC-0021 Open question 1 as its record. The moto table goes into its body, and the RFC cites its ID. The decision then waits where an S3 driver author will see it.

options.label: Line in BK-432
options.description: No new item. BK-432's body gets 'Open: RFC-0021 Open question 1 (markers)'. BK-432 closes when spec 003's section lands, though, which is before any S3 driver moves, so the question could close with it unanswered.

options.label: Line in BK-436
options.description: BK-436 (observing each backend's tree) is after BK-432 and already measures backends, so the marker decision rides along with it. That widens BK-436's scope from observing to deciding.

questions.question: The empty-segment rule decides `a//b` and Azure's `a/` as undecodable, but a caller sees them exactly like the S3 marker we left open (`is_folder("a")` is True and the listing is empty). How far should the open question reach?

options.label: All empty-segment shapes (Recommended)
options.description: Open question 1 covers every flat raw key with an empty segment (`a/`, `a//b`, `/a`) on every flat encoding (S3, Azure without HNS, others), and A.2's empty-segment bullet becomes a pointer to it. This is consistent, and it's one decision when the drivers move.

options.label: Trust the encoding now
options.description: Keep the shapes undecodable, and add an A.3 limit saying keyed calls at the parent trust the encoding (as for keys below an item): `is_folder(a)` is T, a write of `a` is InvalidPath, `delete_folder(a)` is DirectoryNotEmpty. That decides the answers now, and markers stay open on S3 only.

questions.question: A.1 hands BK-436 both measuring name equality and how a coarser backend then answers. BK-436 owns only the measuring. How should I close the gap?

options.label: Widen BK-436 (Recommended)
options.description: BK-436's open decision gains: 'and how a backend with coarser name equality answers a Key that only collides'. One item owns the whole question.

options.label: Trim A.1
options.description: A.1 drops 'and how they then answer'. The RFC then says only that the scope is exact equality, and the answering stays unowned until someone measures.
